audit.action: cite a better source for the same coding
audit.reasoning: (1) Quote check: the deciding Volodin 1997 sec. 2.1.2 sentence is verbatim in the held utf-8 reprint (lines 456-458) and I pinned its print page to p. 62 from a page-image scan fetched sources now; the Bobaljik 1997 corroborating sentence is on PDF p. 7 of the re-fetched sources ROA-208. (2) Deciding source is a 1997 encyclopedia grammar sketch by the language's principal grammarian; no phonology monograph or instrumental word-stress study exists that I could find (Crossref, lingbuzz, archive.org, Kulturstiftung Sibirien; Bobaljik 2025 says Itelmen prosody work is 'in its early stages'; Borise & Bobaljik 2026 is phrase-level). Four independent descriptions now on file agree on left-edge/initial accent: Bogoras 1922:680, Stebnitsky 1934:89, Volodin 1997:62, Bobaljik 1997 p.7 and Bobaljik p.c. in Schiering & van der Hulst 2010:523. (3) The key new finding: Stebnitsky 1934 — the one primary source StressTy

sources.quote: Volodin: "The prosodic organization of the word in Itelmen is characterized by an accentual alternation of syllables of the trochaic type (– v – v – v ...). Syllables with a glottal stop receive additional accentual strengthening, cf. below." (– = accented, v = unaccented; trochaic = starting from the first syllable.)

sources.quote: «§ 13. Ударение в ительменском так же как в луораветланском и нымыланском, падает на начало слова, чаще всего на первый или второй слог.» [Stress in Itelmen, as in Chukchi and Koryak, falls on the beginning of the word, most often on the first or second syllable.] This is the source StressTyp2 cites for FINAL stress; it says the opposite. Closes the owner-note fence ('Stebnitsky 1934 unread'; attribution to Stebnitsky confirmed).
